notes.text: For more than 6, set up a second rolling station so two people can roll at once.

move.title: Matchsticks that roll
move.body: Julienne means cutting vegetables into thin, even matchsticks. Today you'll cut carrots and cucumber that way, then roll them up tight in soft rice paper with chicken, noodles, and mint.

why.title: Make a flat side first
why.body: A round carrot rolls under the knife, and a rolling carrot is how fingers get cut. Slice a thin strip off one side and lay the carrot on that flat side. Now it sits still. Almost every vegetable you cut from now on starts this way.

why.title: Why matchsticks
why.body: Thin sticks bend with the roll instead of poking holes in the wrapper. When they're all the same size, they lie side by side in a neat bundle, and every bite gets some crunch.

why.title: Rice paper keeps softening
why.body: Rice paper is a dried sheet of rice flour and water. A quick dip lets it start drinking, and it keeps soaking up the water that's on it while it sits on the towel. Pull it out while it still feels a little stiff. Soak it too long and it goes floppy and tears.

why.title: Gentle bubbles, juicy chicken
why.body: Hard boiling squeezes the juice out of chicken and makes it stringy. Water that barely bubbles cooks it slowly and evenly, so it stays tender. The thermometer tells you when it's safe: 165°F in the thickest part.

wrong.sign: The wrapper tears while you roll
wrong.fix: It soaked too long, or there's too much filling. Use a shorter dip and a little less filling. A torn roll can be wrapped again in a second wrapper.

wrong.sign: The roll is loose and falls apart
wrong.fix: Pull the bottom edge snug over the filling before you fold the sides. Tight from the very first fold makes a tight roll.

wrong.sign: The rolls are stuck together on the plate
wrong.fix: Leave a little space between them. If two are stuck, pull them apart slowly and they'll usually come apart without tearing.

wrong.sign: The carrot sticks are thick and uneven
wrong.fix: Stack fewer planks and slow down. Thin planks make thin sticks, so the first cuts matter most.

quiz.q: Why do you cut a flat side on the carrot first?
choices: So it doesn't roll under the knife
quiz.explain: A flat side keeps the carrot still, so the knife goes where you mean it to.

quiz.q: The rice paper still feels a bit stiff after its dip. What do you do?
choices: Put it back in the water for a minute
quiz.explain: It keeps softening on the towel. By the time the filling is on, it's ready to roll.

steps.text: Use the tongs to put the chicken in the saucepan. Add {qty:salt} salt and enough cold water to cover the chicken by about an inch.
steps.tip: Starting in cold water means nothing splashes when the chicken goes in.

steps.text: Wash the tongs in hot, soapy water. Wash your hands with soap, and wipe anything the raw chicken or its package touched.
Set the pan over medium-high heat. When the water starts to boil, turn the heat down to low and put the lid on.
steps.look: Big bubbles rolling across the whole top of the water.

steps.text: Let the chicken cook on low. The water should barely bubble.
steps.tip: Cut the vegetables while it cooks.

steps.text: Peel the carrots. Cut them into pieces about 3 inches long, about as long as your pointer finger.
steps.tip: Peel away from your hand, and keep your fingers behind the blade.

steps.text: Slice a thin strip off one long side of each carrot piece. Turn it so it sits on that flat side.
steps.tip: Hold the carrot with your hand shaped like a claw: fingertips tucked under, knuckles in front. The flat of the knife slides along your knuckles.

steps.text: Slice each piece the long way into thin planks, about as thick as a coin.
steps.look: Flat, even planks you can almost see light through.

steps.text: Stack 2 or 3 planks and julienne them: slice the stack the long way into thin matchsticks.
steps.tip: A short stack is easier to hold still than a tall one.

steps.text: Cut the cucumber into 3-inch pieces. Make a flat side, cut planks, and julienne them the same way. Leave out the soft, seedy middle.
steps.tip: The seedy middle makes the rolls soggy. Snack on it instead.

steps.text: Turn off the heat. Lift a piece of chicken out with the tongs and slide the thermometer into the thickest part. It needs to read at least 165°F. If it doesn't, put it back for 3 more minutes and check again.
Move the chicken to the plate to cool. Carefully pour the hot water down the sink.
steps.tip: Pour away from your body, and let an adult take this one if the pan is heavy.

steps.text: Fill the saucepan with fresh water and bring it to a boil. Turn off the heat, add the noodles, and stir so they don't clump. Let them soak until soft.
steps.look: Soft and white all the way through, with no hard center.

steps.text: Set the colander in the sink and pour the noodles into it. Run cold water over them until they're cool, shake off the water, and put them in the big bowl.
Wash the lettuce and pat it dry. Tear the leaves into pieces about the size of your hand, and tear out the thick, crunchy rib from the middle.
Wash and dry the cutting board. Slice the cooled chicken across the grain into thin slices.
Put the peanut butter, hoisin sauce, and lime juice in the small bowl. Stir with the fork, adding warm water a spoonful at a time, until it's smooth and thin enough to dip.
steps.look: Smooth, and it drips slowly off the fork.

steps.text: Set up a rolling station. Pour warm water into the shallow dish. Wet a kitchen towel, wring it out, and spread it flat on the board. Line up the lettuce, noodles, carrots, cucumber, herbs, and chicken in that order, close by.
steps.tip: With everything in reach, you can roll with your hands still wet.

steps.text: Slide one rice paper wrapper into the warm water and count to 2. Lift it out and lay it flat on the towel. It will still feel a little stiff.
On the third of the wrapper closest to you, lay a piece of lettuce, a small handful of noodles, a few carrot and cucumber sticks, and some herbs. Lay 2 or 3 slices of chicken on top.
steps.tip: Less filling than you think. A small bundle rolls tighter.

steps.text: Fold the bottom edge of the wrapper up and over the filling, and pull it snug. Fold the left and right sides over the filling. Roll it away from you, keeping it tight, until it's sealed.
steps.look: A tight, see-through roll with the colors showing.

steps.text: Set the roll on a serving plate with the seam underneath. Make the rest the same way, going back through the last three steps. Don't let the rolls touch.
steps.tip: Change the warm water if it gets cool. Cool water softens the wrappers too slowly.

steps.text: Serve the rolls whole or cut in half on a slant, with the sauce for dipping. If they have to wait, cover them with a damp towel so they don't dry out.
